'''JoAnna H. Mendoza''' (born 1975 or 1976) is an American politician and military veteran who is the [[U.S. representative]]-elect for [[Arizona's 6th congressional district]]. A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]], Mendoza beat incumbent [[Republican (United States)|Republican]] [[Juan Ciscomani]] in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Arizona#District 6|2026 election]].

Mendoza served in the [[United States Navy]] from 1994 to 1997. She later joined the [[United States Marine Corps|Marine Corps]], completing two tours in [[War in Iraq|Iraq]] and one in [[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|Afghanistan]] before leaving active duty service in 2016.

== Early life and education ==
JoAnna H. Mendoza<ref name="Legi"/> was born in [[Eloy, Arizona]],<ref name="Draws">{{cite web |last1=Gersony |first1=Laura |title=Rep. Juan Ciscomani draws an early Democratic challenger for congressional seat |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/politics/elections/2025/02/12/rep-juan-ciscomani-draws-an-early-democratic-challenger/78431202007/ |website=The Arizona Republic |access-date=8 June 2026}}</ref> in 1975 or 1976,<ref name="Roll">{{cite web |last1=Altimari |first1=Daniela |title=2026 could be breakout year for blue-collar Democratic women |url=https://rollcall.com/2025/10/08/working-class-women-democrats-midterm-elections/ |website=Roll Call |access-date=8 June 2026 |date=8 October 2025}}</ref> the oldest of five children in a [[Catholic]] family.<ref name="NYT">{{cite web |last1=Medina |first1=Jennifer |title=A New Worry for Republicans: Latino Catholics Offended by Trump |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/24/us/politics/trump-pope-latino-voters.html |website=The New York Times |access-date=8 June 2026 |date=24 April 2026}}</ref><ref name="Lean">{{cite web |title=Gunnery Sergeant JoAnna Mendoza |url=https://leanin.org/stories/gunnery-sergeant-joanna-mendoza#! |website=Lean In |access-date=8 June 2026 |language=en}}</ref> At eight years old, Mendoza began working as a cotton picker with her parents, both [[Mexico|Mexican]] immigrants.<ref name="LVF">{{cite web |title=Progressive group endorses four Latinas in competitive House districts |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/latino/latino-victory-endorsement-latinas-congress-democrats-rcna222072 |website=NBC News |access-date=8 June 2026 |language=en |date=30 July 2025}}</ref><ref name="Mother"/><ref name="Eloy">{{cite web |title=Democrat JoAnna Mendoza hopes to unseat Rep. Juan Ciscomani in Southern Az's CD6 |url=https://www.tucsonsentinel.com/local/report/040826_mendoza_profile/democrat-joanna-mendoza-hopes-unseat-rep-juan-ciscomani-southern-azs-cd6/ |website=Tucson Sentinel |access-date=8 June 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2013, Mendoza graduated from the [[American Military University]] with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in [[intelligence studies]].<ref name="Ballot">{{cite web |title=JoAnna Mendoza |url=https://ballotpedia.org/JoAnna_Mendoza |website=Ballotpedia |access-date=8 June 2026 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Legi"/> She attained a [[Master of Science in Leadership]] from [[Grand Canyon University]] in 2019.<ref name="Ballot"/><ref name="Legi">{{cite web |title=JoAnna Mendoza |url=https://www.legistorm.com/person/bio/303546/JoAnna_H_Mendoza.html |website=LegiStorm |access-date=8 June 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

== Military career ==

Mendoza joined the military at age 17,<ref name="Tucson">{{cite web |title=Marine vet JoAnna Mendoza challenges Ciscomani in AZ-6 |url=https://www.tucsonspotlight.org/marine-vet-joanna-mendoza-challenges-ciscomani-in-az-6/ |website=Tucson Spotlight |access-date=8 June 2026 |language=en |date=17 March 2026}}</ref> serving in the [[United States Navy]],<ref name="Ballot"/> where she worked as a boiler tech on the [[USS Samuel Gompers]] from 1994 to 1997.<ref name="Ballot"/><ref name="Eloy"/>

The following year, she joined the [[United States Marine Corps|Marine Corps]],<ref name="Advocate"/> where she was a [[gunnery sergeant]] and [[drill instructor]] until 2016.<ref name="Advocate"/><ref name="Tucson"/><ref name="Ballot"/>

In the Marine Corps, Mendoza led combat tours during both the [[Iraq War]] and the [[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]].<ref name="Tucson"/> She was deployed twice to Iraq and once to Afghanistan.<ref name="Ballot"/><ref name="Eloy"/>

== Professional career ==
After retiring from the Marine Corps, Mendoza was appointed as a governing board member of her local school district in [[Red Rock, Pinal County, Arizona|Red Rock]].<ref name="Ballot"/> She worked as the veteran services representative in the office of U.S. representative [[Tom O'Halleran]] from May 2018 to July 2019,<ref name="Anti"/><ref name="Legi"/> when she became veteran outreach coordinator at [[Pima Community College]].<ref name="Legi"/> 

In 2020, Mendoza ran to represent [[Arizona's 11th legislative district|Arizona's 11th state senate district]] as a [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]].<ref name="Eloy"/> She lost to incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Vince Leach]] in the general election, receiving 45.6% of the vote.<ref name="Ballot"/>

Mendoza rejoined O'Halleran's campaign staff in January 2021, working as deputy district director for a year before becoming his campaign manager.<ref name="Legi"/> After O'Halleran lost re-election in 2022, Mendoza worked as the executive director for the Arizona Center for Economic Progress, an economic think tank.<ref name="Eloy"/> She also served as executive director of veterans organization Vets Forward.<ref name="Eloy"/>

== 2026 congressional campaign ==
{{Also|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Arizona#District 6}}

Mendoza was the Democratic nominee in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Arizona#District 6|2026 election]] for [[Arizona's 6th congressional district]].<ref name="Central">{{cite web |last1=Luberto |first1=Amanda |title=Arizona's next big political fights emerge as Trump's approval dips |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/politics/elections/2025/10/15/arizona-politics-house-races-2026-who-is-running/86591940007/ |website=The Arizona Republic |access-date=8 June 2026}}</ref> The district, represented by [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Juan Ciscomani]], was viewed as a competitive toss-up.<ref name="Central"/><ref name="Fund"/> She was endorsed by the [[Blue Dog Coalition|Blue Dog PAC]].<ref>https://bluedogdems.com/joanna-mendoza/</ref>

In the first quarter of 2026, Mendoza's campaign raised [[USD|US]]$2.3 million.<ref name="Fund">{{cite web |title=Democratic House challenger in Arizona pulls in $2.3M quarterly haul |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/04/03/democratic-house-challenger-joanna-mendoza-2026-fundraising-00856581 |website=POLITICO |access-date=8 June 2026 |language=en |date=3 April 2026}}</ref> [[Arizona Public Media]] described Mendoza as a "prolific fundraiser".<ref name="Anti">{{cite web |title="Anti-democratic": Arizona Democrat criticizes party's program boosting certain primary candidates |url=https://news.azpm.org/s/102821-anti-democratic-arizona-democrat-criticizes-partys-program-boosting-certain-primary-candidates/ |website=AZPM |access-date=8 June 2026 |language=en}}</ref> She won the November 3, 2026, election.<ref>{{cite web |title=JoAnna Mendoza wins Arizona House seat, flipping key district for Dems |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6178905-democrat-mendoza-wins-arizona-district-6/ |website=The Hill |access-date=4 November 2026}}</ref>

== Political views ==
Mendoza is a former Republican, but voted for [[Hillary Clinton]] in the [[2016 United States presidential election|2016 presidential election]].<ref name="Eloy"/>

== Personal life ==
A single [[queer]] mother,<ref name="Advocate"/><ref name="Tucson"/> Mendoza lives in [[Red Rock, Pinal County, Arizona|Red Rock]] with her son, Aidan.<ref name="Eloy"/><ref name="Mother">{{cite web |title=JoAnna Mendoza on being a single mom, a Marine veteran, and a first-time congressional candidate in Southern Arizona |url=https://www.mother.ly/career-money/work-and-motherhood/joanna-mendoza/ |website=Motherly |access-date=8 June 2026 |language=en |date=6 May 2026}}</ref><ref name="Advocate">{{cite web |title=Queer vet JoAnna Mendoza brings Marine grit to AZ politics |url=https://www.advocate.com/politics/joanna-mendoza-arizona-congressional-run |website=Advocate |access-date=8 June 2026 |language=en}}</ref> Mendoza was raised as a [[Catholic]], but is no longer practicing.<ref name="NYT"/>

Alongside [[Rebecca Bennett (politician)|Rebecca Bennett]], [[Cait Conley]], and [[Maura Sullivan]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Why 'Hellcats' could be the answer to Democrats troubles |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/06/12/sherrill-spanberger-military-veterans-2026-00401395 |website=POLITICO |access-date=8 June 2026 |language=en |date=12 June 2025}}</ref> she is a member of the Hell Cats, a group of Democratic female veterans who ran in competitive districts in 2026.<ref>{{cite web |title=Four Female Veterans Running for Congress Launch: "The Hell Cats"  - Insider NJ |url=https://www.insidernj.com/press-release/four-female-veterans-running-for-congress-launch-the-hell-cats/ |website=Insider NJ |access-date=8 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Walsh |first1=Joan |title=Hell Cats vs. Hegseth |url=https://www.thenation.com/article/society/hellcats-hegseth-democrats-military-vets/ |website=The Nation |access-date=8 June 2026 |date=13 January 2026}}</ref>
